title: A portable, broad-spectrum emergency diagnostic system

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a portable system that helps clinicians distinguish several urgent, treatable causes of collapse or severe illness when the cause is initially unclear. It would support decisions near the patient, including locations far from hospital imaging and laboratories. Its defining capability would be reliable discrimination among different emergencies despite overlapping symptoms, early disease and coexisting conditions.

Concept synthesis: The system would need to obtain and combine enough information about the patient's anatomy and physiology to guide emergency decisions without specialist imaging infrastructure. The proposal does not prescribe a particular sensor, scanner, blood test or software architecture. A collection of existing tests would qualify only if the integrated system demonstrated the intended clinical capability. Perfect accuracy for every condition is not assumed; useful performance would include recognizing uncertainty and identifying when further investigation or referral is necessary.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: If the system achieved broad diagnostic coverage, reliable performance, portability and low cost, it could move consequential emergency diagnostic decisions closer to where illness occurs. Its direct contribution would be earlier identification or sufficiently reliable exclusion of several immediately treatable emergencies, helping clinicians choose initial treatment, transport urgency and destination. Affordability and this breadth of performance are objectives of the proposal, not demonstrated properties.

A narrower precedent illustrates why reducing infrastructure requirements matters. The 2024 CDMRP announcement describes a handheld traumatic brain injury blood test whose whole-blood workflow eliminates the centrifugation required by an earlier plasma workflow. The announcement presents this simplification as enabling testing outside clinical settings and potentially supporting military triage. That example supports the practical value of portable diagnostic workflows, while leaving the proposed multi-emergency capability unestablished.

Conditional downstream possibilities include faster access to appropriate treatment, fewer avoidable transfers and better routing to facilities with the necessary capabilities. These benefits would depend on the availability of effective treatment, transport, trained users and functioning referral systems. A correct diagnosis alone does not deliver treatment, and false reassurance or unnecessary intervention could offset gains. The revolutionary advance would therefore be demonstrated breadth and usefulness in emergency decisions, rather than portability by itself.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed unsolved capability: The target is dependable discrimination among multiple hidden emergencies in patients who have not already been sorted into a specific diagnostic pathway. Early presentations may provide weak signals, different diseases may produce similar symptoms, and more than one condition may be present. The supplied evidence does not establish whether a system already achieves this combined capability across the field, so its present-day absence remains an open question rather than a demonstrated fact.

Engineering synthesis: A central barrier is acquiring sufficient diagnostic information within the practical constraints of emergency care. The system would need informative anatomical and physiological measurements while limiting equipment size, power requirements, specimen preparation, operator dependence and time to an actionable result. The appropriate combination of measurements remains unspecified. The supplied sources do not establish that every successful design must use a particular mixture of imaging and biomarkers.

Scientific and clinical synthesis: Combining measurements must yield dependable clinical decisions, not simply a larger volume of data. Development would need to address competing explanations for abnormal findings, early disease, simultaneous conditions, incomplete measurements and changes in the populations being tested. The system would also need meaningful uncertainty reporting and safe handling of inconclusive results. Accuracy for one diagnosis or one selected population would not establish performance across undifferentiated emergencies.

The documented TBI component illustrates a concrete workflow barrier and a bounded advance: replacing plasma preparation with whole-blood testing reduced dependence on centrifugation. Extending this kind of practical simplification to a broad emergency diagnostic system would still require evidence that the resulting measurements and combined decisions remain sufficiently informative and reliable.

current_state.text: A documented component is the i-STAT TBI cartridge used on a handheld instrument. A CDMRP announcement dated April 22, 2024 reports FDA clearance for adults over 18, using whole blood collected within 24 hours after suspected injury, to help clinicians assess the need for head CT. The supplied research also attributes a 15-minute result time to this release; the validated review confirms the population, specimen, timing window and intended CT-assessment role, but does not separately verify that turnaround figure. This is a targeted diagnostic aid, not evidence of broad diagnosis of undifferentiated collapse.

The evidence available for that component is an official announcement whose relevant HTML text was assessed in the supplied review. A pivotal clinical trial report and regulatory labeling were not inspected there. The release supports the reported clearance and intended workflow, but does not by itself establish condition-specific diagnostic accuracy, improved patient outcomes or applicability outside the stated adult post-injury context.

The supplied research identifies a purported systematic review and meta-analysis of portable low- and ultra-low-field MRI for acute ischemic stroke, attributed to Pence and colleagues and dated July 16, 2026. It reports pooled sensitivity of 73.3% and specificity of 79.3% across six comparative studies, substantial heterogeneity and a caution against standalone stroke rule-out. These details remain unverified in the supplied review: although the research says an abstract was inspected on an earlier pass, the retained PubMed text available to the reviewer was only a cookie-access challenge and contained neither article identity nor results. The figures are preserved here as unresolved research-reported claims, not established performance estimates. This access limitation does not show that the reported findings are false.

The supplied material does not demonstrate the proposed integrated system, its affordability or its clinical outcome benefits. It also does not establish that no such system exists: the freshness record supplied to the review was empty, the MRI content could not be assessed, and the verified diagnostic announcement concerns a 2024 component. Consequently, the review could not establish the state of the entire field at its November 1, 2026 cutoff. An additional PDF retained alongside the CDMRP release concerned consumer reviewer nominations and provides no diagnostic evidence; that mismatch does not undermine the relevant HTML announcement.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: First define the emergencies the system is intended to distinguish and the decisions it is intended to support. A prospective protocol should specify condition-specific performance thresholds, appropriate reference standards, endpoints and acceptable harm margins before evaluation. These would be proposed requirements for the intended use, not established universal standards. The protocol should also distinguish identifying a condition, ruling it out and recommending further assessment, because those uses impose different demands.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified intended uses and condition-specific diagnostic performance requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed diagnostic validation: Recruit consecutive, undifferentiated patients rather than only patients already known to have particular diseases. Studies should evaluate adults and children and include urban, rural and resource-limited settings where use is intended. They should report condition-specific accuracy, uncertainty, inconclusive results and failure modes, including performance in early presentations and coexisting disease. Positive findings would establish the breadth demonstrated in those studies; finite testing could not establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Condition-specific accuracy in consecutive, undifferentiated patients across intended settings

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical validation: Independent teams should reproduce clinically useful performance across multiple sites, operators and relevant patient groups. Evaluation should document time to an actionable result, specimen preparation, power and equipment needs, training requirements, operating costs and the frequency of failed measurements. Claims of portability and affordability should be tied to explicit operating conditions and measured resource requirements.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduced clinical performance with measured operating resource requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical benefit demonstration: Controlled implementation studies should establish whether using the integrated system improves meaningful outcomes or timely appropriate care without unacceptable harms from missed diagnoses, unnecessary treatment or inappropriate transport decisions. Those studies should specify how uncertain results lead to further investigation or referral and account for the treatment and transport resources available. Strong diagnostic performance would be necessary evidence, but would not alone demonstrate patient benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled implementation improves outcomes or timely care without unacceptable harms

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: EMR-01, Reversible emergency metabolic suspension, and EMR-02, Neurologically intact recovery after prolonged untreated cardiac arrest, concern preserving or restoring patients during extreme physiological failure. EMR-05 could potentially inform recognition and routing if relevant diagnostic capabilities were validated. Its contribution is diagnostic decision support; it does not itself establish reversible suspension, resuscitation or neurological recovery.

Roster-based synthesis: EMR-03, Field treatment that safely stops inaccessible internal bleeding, and EMR-04, Inexpensive, universally compatible emergency blood replacement, address interventions for bleeding and circulatory compromise. A broad diagnostic system might help identify patients needing those interventions or distinguish bleeding from other causes of collapse. Detecting the problem would remain distinct from stopping hemorrhage or replacing blood safely.

Roster-based synthesis: EMR-06, Rapid reversal of septic shock and its harmful host response, and EMR-07, Broad-spectrum emergency antidote platform, share the challenge of acting quickly when symptoms may have several causes. EMR-05 could potentially help identify infection-related shock or poisoning and guide escalation. Its proposed diagnostic breadth does not imply the ability to reverse the host response in sepsis or neutralize multiple toxins.

Roster-based synthesis: EMR-08, Non-surgical rescue oxygenation for otherwise unmanageable airways, concerns an immediate physiological rescue capability. EMR-05 could overlap through assessment of oxygenation problems or their causes, but diagnostic information does not itself provide rescue oxygenation. Any implementation would need to fit urgent care workflows without delaying necessary intervention.

Roster-based synthesis: EMR-09, Effective early prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder after emergency care, and EMR-10, Rapid, potent non-opioid treatment for severe acute pain, concern prevention and treatment within or following emergency care. Diagnostic clarification could potentially inform management, but neither prevention of later psychological injury nor effective analgesia follows automatically from identifying an acute medical cause.

Roster-based synthesis: EMR-11, Acute rescue and repair of injured vital tissue, concerns therapeutic rescue and repair. EMR-05 could potentially help identify injury and prioritize referral if its validated condition set included the relevant tissue damage. Detecting injury, rescuing threatened tissue and repairing established damage remain separate capabilities.

Conceptual synthesis: Across the roster, EMR-05 is an enabling diagnostic capability with overlap in imaging, blood biomarkers, biomedical engineering and clinical decision support. Its identity depends on demonstrated integration across emergency decisions. It remains distinct from each therapeutic concept even where better diagnosis could make a treatment more timely or appropriately targeted.

unresolved_issues: Whether an existing system already achieves the proposed integrated capability remains unestablished by the supplied evidence; field-wide status at the review's November 1, 2026 cutoff was not verified.

The identity, publication date, pooled accuracy estimates, six-study count, heterogeneity and standalone rule-out caution attributed to the 2026 MRI review require accessible article content. The retained PubMed artifact contains only an access challenge.

The review recommended removing the unverified MRI numerical results. They were instead retained solely as explicitly unresolved research-reported claims to preserve quantitative detail as requested; they are not used as established evidence.
The 15-minute TBI turnaround figure is attributed by the research to the official release but is not separately confirmed in the validated review.
The supplied review did not inspect pivotal TBI trial evidence or regulatory labeling, leaving detailed accuracy, labeling and outcome questions beyond the verified announcement unresolved.
The intended condition set, clinical decisions, measurement architecture, performance thresholds, outcome endpoints and acceptable harm margins remain to be defined.

Portability, affordability, pediatric applicability, performance in early or coexisting disease, and improved outcomes are objectives requiring demonstration rather than established attributes of the proposed system.

brief.title: Finding the cause of a medical emergency anywhere
possible: When someone collapses or becomes severely ill far from a hospital, clinicians could use a portable system to distinguish several urgent, treatable causes. It would help them choose initial treatment and decide how urgently—and where—the patient needs to travel.
why: Earlier answers could bring appropriate care closer to people in rural areas and places with limited medical resources. They could also spare patients avoidable transfers and help route them to facilities equipped to treat them.

sources.showed: Their review examined portable magnetic resonance imaging, which uses magnetic fields to make images. Accuracy varied across studies of strokes caused by blocked blood flow, and the scans missed some small injuries.
sources.quote: corresponding to approximately one in four confirmed infarcts being missed, with missed lesions generally small or sub-centimetric.
sources.cited_for: Portable brain scanning offers a limited precedent for bringing emergency diagnosis to the bedside.
sources.not_established: These scans cannot reliably exclude a stroke on their own or establish the ability to distinguish among multiple emergencies.

sources.who: Abbott Laboratories, Ronald Hayes, Kevin Wang and collaborators
sources.showed: They developed a handheld blood test that detects proteins released after brain injury. It helps clinicians assess whether adults need a head scan and uses whole blood without separating it first.
sources.quote: The i-STAT TBI cartridge works on Abbott's hand-held i-STAT Alinity® instrument and produces lab-quality results within 15 minutes.
sources.cited_for: Removing blood preparation steps can make a targeted emergency test practical outside a clinical setting.
sources.not_established: A test for suspected brain injury does not establish broad emergency diagnosis or improved patient outcomes.

shown: Abbott's handheld blood test can help assess the need for a head scan after suspected brain injury in adults. Portable brain scanners have also detected strokes at the bedside, but miss some cases. These are narrower capabilities than distinguishing several possible causes of unexplained severe illness.
missing: Reliable discrimination among several emergencies in patients whose symptoms have not already pointed to a particular diagnosis needs demonstration.
Independent studies need to establish practical use, including equipment, power, training, preparation time and cost.
Controlled studies need to establish better care without unacceptable harm from missed illness, unnecessary treatment or poor transport decisions.

milestones.label: Clear uses and standards set before testing
milestones.explanation: A study plan would have to define target emergencies, supported decisions, accuracy requirements and acceptable harms before testing. This would distinguish finding a condition from excluding it or seeking further assessment.

milestones.label: Accuracy across patients with unexplained emergencies
milestones.explanation: Studies enrolling patients as they arrive would have to establish accuracy across intended ages and settings, including early illness, simultaneous conditions and inconclusive results. This would test the system's breadth.

milestones.label: Independent results with measured practical needs
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce useful performance across sites and users while measuring time, equipment, power, training, costs and failures. This would establish reliability and practical operating needs.

milestones.label: Better care without unacceptable harm
milestones.explanation: Controlled studies would have to show better outcomes or timelier appropriate care without unacceptable harms, including when results are uncertain. This would establish patient benefit under real treatment and transport constraints.

uncertain: Whether an existing system already achieves the full combined capability remains an open question.
Which measurements would provide enough information within the limits of portable emergency care remains unclear.

page.title: Portable differential diagnosis of acute illness
page.definition: A portable system combines measurements taken where a patient receives care and helps a clinician distinguish urgent, treatable causes of the same symptoms. For example, heart and lung findings can help distinguish causes of sudden breathlessness such as heart failure and pneumonia. The system must give condition-specific results before the clinician has chosen which disease to investigate, without relying on a hospital laboratory or imaging department.

goal.need: An estimated 47% of people worldwide have little or no access to safe, affordable, quality-assured diagnostics. Sudden breathlessness can signal heart failure or pneumonia, and the examination may leave the cause unclear while blood tests and chest imaging are pending. In one trial of patients with signs of respiratory failure, adding bedside heart and lung ultrasound to standard assessment increased appropriate treatment prescriptions at four hours from 65.7% to 79.3%. Agreement with the final diagnosis was similar in both groups.

figures.caption: CT-scanner availability reported by WHO.
figures.note: Health-system availability figures; these are not device performance requirements.

statements.context: The Qualcomm Tricorder XPRIZE concerned consumer testing for a defined set of 13 health conditions and monitoring five vital health metrics.

statements.context: The project specified a point-of-care platform that would combine measurements of proteins and genetic material to distinguish infectious causes of fever.

completion.title: FDA authorizes a portable integrated system for multi-emergency differential diagnosis.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a 510(k) clearance, grants a De Novo request, or approves a premarket approval application whose labeling explicitly covers the integrated portable system's differential diagnosis of multiple urgent, treatable causes of initially undifferentiated acute illness in specified near-patient settings. Separate component authorizations, vital-sign monitoring alone, and authorization confined to a single disease-specific pathway do not satisfy this Atlas-defined scope.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; FDA defines the marketing pathways, but no external document defining this integrated emergency completion scope was identified.
completion.basis: Searches of WHO diagnostic-access documents, FDA development and marketing guidance, and Qualcomm Tricorder XPRIZE materials found no completion criterion for undifferentiated multi-emergency diagnosis. The prize concerned a defined consumer condition panel. Authorization for the integrated emergency intended use supplies an auditable endpoint without inventing accuracy, weight or cost limits. It does not establish reduced mortality or affordability.

milestones.title: An integrated laboratory prototype produces diagnostic outputs for its stated emergency conditions.
milestones.criterion: In controlled laboratory testing, an operating prototype acquires and combines measurements and returns condition-specific diagnostic results for the emergency conditions it is designed to distinguish.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas defines the condition-specific output requirement. FDA describes controlled laboratory testing of prototypes but gives no acceptance limits for this integrated emergency use.

milestones.title: An early feasibility study demonstrates proof of principle and assesses initial clinical safety.
milestones.criterion: An early clinical study in intended patients demonstrates that the integrated system can produce its intended diagnostic outputs and provides initial clinical safety data for that use.
milestones.set_by: FDA, early-feasibility-study guidance, section 11; a general device-development criterion, originally framed for significant-risk devices, without an emergency-specific numerical acceptance threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early feasibility studies may be used to provide proof of principle and initial clinical safety data.

milestones.title: A pivotal study supports the integrated system's intended emergency diagnostic use.
milestones.criterion: A pivotal study evaluates the integrated system in its intended patients and settings. For each target condition, it compares the system's output with a prespecified clinical reference standard that establishes the patient's status independently of that output. The findings support the safety and effectiveness of the system for its specified emergency diagnostic use.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Design Considerations for Pivotal Clinical Investigations for Medical Devices, glossary and section 8; a general diagnostic-device evidentiary criterion, without a published multi-emergency performance cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: In a diagnostic clinical performance study, each subject is assessed for the target condition, using a clinical reference standard.

milestones.title: A feasibility study of the near-final system provides the evidence needed to plan pivotal testing.
milestones.criterion: When a traditional feasibility study is used, it evaluates a near-final or final integrated system in patients and provides preliminary safety and effectiveness information sufficient to plan the pivotal study for its intended emergency use.
milestones.set_by: FDA, early feasibility study guidance, section 3. Traditional feasibility is a distinct, optional clinical stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: capture preliminary safety and effectiveness information on a near-final or final device design to adequately plan an appropriate pivotal study.

not_found: No published condition panel, accuracy cutoff, weight limit or cost ceiling was found for the full undifferentiated multi-emergency capability.
No registered pivotal protocol or FDA marketing authorization was identified for the full integrated intended use; field-wide absence remains unestablished.
The original Qualcomm Tricorder XPRIZE competition-guidelines PDF could not be opened.
No regulator, professional society or funder statement was identified that endorses or disputes the full integrated use across undifferentiated acute presentations.

results.finding: In approximately 2,000 patients with suspected mild TBI, the ALERT-TBI biomarker test predicted CT-detectable brain injury within 12 hours after injury.
results.detail: Participants entered a suspected-TBI pathway. The release gives no numerical accuracy estimate.
results.quote: trial of approximately 2,000 subjects with suspected mild TBI successfully demonstrated that the blood-based biomarker test accurately predicted CT-scan-detectable brain injuries within 12 hours after injury, according to Wang.

results.finding: FeverDisk tested 15 cartridges in controlled spiking experiments and distinguished 3 bacterial causes of acute fever.
results.detail: Twelve disks tested all three bacterial targets together. Three additional disks tested S. Paratyphi A alone. The broader panel had no demonstrated positive Zika detection.
results.quote:
Twelve FeverDisks were used for S. Typhi, S. Paratyphi A and S. pneumoniae,
with 3 additional FeverDisks used for S. Paratyphi A only.

results.finding: FeverDisk detected microscopy-confirmed falciparum malaria in the only acute-fever patient tested with a fresh sample (n=1).
results.detail: The fresh sample came from a patient whose malaria had already been identified by microscopy. The aggregate agreement was measured per assay across the laboratory series.
results.quote:
During the days of the tests, one patient presented with acute fever, and after clinical exami-
nation was found Pf positive based on microscopy. A blood sample (coded as “Sample X”,
Table 2) was taken and immediately tested in the FeverDisk, which yielded Pf and Pspp posi-
tive results (Fig 6).

results.finding: Among 1,586 febrile children managed with e-POCT, 0.6% had a severe adverse event by day 30.
results.detail: The study tested the system's classifications and management recommendations during the initial outpatient consultation.
results.quote:
The proportion of severe adverse events was 0.6% in the e-POCT arm compared
with 1.5% in the ALMANACH arm (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.20, 0.87, p = 0.02).

results.finding: In 3,169 febrile children analyzed per protocol, e-POCT reduced the relative risk of day-7 clinical failure by 43% versus ALMANACH.
results.detail: The relative risk reduction came from a non-prespecified superiority analysis. The primary analysis tested non-inferiority on clinical failure.
results.quote:
There was a 43% reduction in relative risk for clinical failure in the e-POCT arm com-
pared to the ALMANACH control arm.

results.finding: In 28,759 evaluable initial pediatric consultations, ePOCT+ had an adjusted relative risk of 0.97 for day 7 clinical failure versus usual care.
results.detail: Day 7 clinical failure was based on caregiver-reported lack of recovery or improvement, or unscheduled hospitalization. Some facilities ran point-of-care tests in their own laboratories.
results.quote: The coprimary outcome of day 7 clinical failure was noninferior in ePOCT+ facilities compared to usual care facilities (adjusted relative risk 0.97, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.10).

results.finding: Visby Respiratory Health Test in 1,501 symptomatic patients showed 97.2% positive agreement with laboratory RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2.
results.detail: The device simultaneously differentiates three viral targets. The clinical study took place in urgent care and family care clinics and measured assay agreement.

results.finding: A portable electromagnetic brain scanner classified ischaemic versus hemorrhagic stroke with 98% accuracy in 50 patients with confirmed stroke.
results.detail: CT or MRI served as the reference. The reported accuracy covers the full cohort, including the first 12 patients whose scans were used to train some of the algorithms.
results.quote: The device classification was observed to demonstrate an ability to differentiate between hemorrhagic and ischaemic stroke with an overall accuracy of 98% in the full sample (50).

results.finding: The 10-port microwave prototype classified ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and no stroke with 98.1% accuracy on 220 phantom measurements, per the methods.
results.detail: The methods identify the 220-measurement M2 dataset as the test set. The Results section describes the roles of M1 and M2 inconsistently. Outside the antenna plane, weaker signals made stroke-type classification unreliable.
results.quote: The overall classification accuracy reached 98.1%, corresponding to a Cohen’s kappa value of 0.95.
